_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-26 · A day on one thing: getting a new draft of the regulation that governs credit for prior learning — Title 5 section 55050 — ready for the Chancellor's Office, now that SB 135 has put credit for prior learning into the Education Code. The finding is that a redraft is the wrong shape. A revised 55050 was already adopted by the Board of Governors on 12 August, and the numbering in it is Sam's own from last November, so it is not a rival version — it is the same section with the substance left out. Its drafting simply finished three weeks before the new law took effect, which is the whole argument: nobody erred, and the regulation now has to be brought into line with the statute it operates under. Five amendments, nothing renumbered, delivered as a Word file with real tracked changes and checked by machine against the adopted text. Earlier the same day, the memory feature: its written briefing was reading 34 of 188 entries and picking them by whichever had been edited most recently.
_status: Everything is merged. The amendment package and the tracked-changes file are ready to take to the Chancellor's Office. Nothing left on it is drafting — four items below are judgment calls or facts only Sam can supply. Nothing was written to the regulation, the register, or anyone else's system; every document here is a proposal.

items.text: The Title 5 55050 package is ready to take to the Chancellor's Office: a Word file with real tracked changes against the version the Board of Governors adopted on 12 August, plus a Regulatory Action Proposal in the same format as your November one. Five changes, and nothing is renumbered. The order to raise them in is in the cover argument doc — lead with the compliance gap, then the timing fact (the drafting finished 19 June, the new law took effect 13 July, so nobody erred), then the remedy, and name our own two stretches before anyone else finds them.

One judgment call worth making before the meeting: whether the four policy items from your November draft — the Credit grade symbol, no fee for assessment, credit against program requirements, and folding two exam sections together — go in the same filing or separately. The recommendation is separately, because those four were argued last November and lost, and bundling them lets a reader treat the whole package as reopening a settled negotiation. The fee one carries an Academic Senate resolution and is the strongest candidate to file on its own soon after.

A thirty-second check somebody with the Education Code open can do: is section 88782 the California Career Passport Program? The adopted regulation cites it, so our amendment mirrors it either way — but your November proposal cited 88792(b)(1) in one place while describing 88782 in another, so one of them is a typo. If 88782 turns out to be wrong that is a defect in the adopted regulation and its own separate correction, not something to slip into this package.

Three blanks in the Regulatory Action Proposal that are yours to fill and that no session should invent: the Executive Sponsor, the Staff Lead, and the timeline against the 2026-27 calendar. Worth noting when you set the dates — the two duties the new law puts on every campus are in force now, so the gap between today and adoption is time in which Title 5 does not tell districts about them.

Separate from the regulation and probably bigger. The new law makes every dollar of implementation funding conditional on 'the metrics described in paragraph (1)' — and paragraph (1) describes four goals and supplies no metrics at all. Somebody has to define them, and the Implementation Funding model is the only college-by-college quantification of those goals that exists. It already covers access and completion, and the pilot-project one is satisfied because MAP is named in the statute. Career advancement is the gap you said you would cover through CPL Projects and the Credential Registry. This needs no rulemaking, which is exactly its advantage — keep it out of the amendment conversation.

The memory entries are now readable end to end in plain English — 202 were rewritten, and there are no entries left without plain text, none with developer jargon, and no British spellings. The hopper of unreviewed entries is worth an afternoon whenever you have one. Two small things still need you: one entry is marked stale but still carries a verification stamp, which needs your go to clear, and 26 verified entries do not name who verified them.

The nightly load of the MAP custom reports failed: MAP returned the student-details dataset twice and left out the exhibit-by-catalog-year one entirely, so the run stopped rather than publishing a partial picture — which is the gate working. Needs a look at whether the report itself was renamed on MAP's side.

None of the 20 entries in the policy register cite the new Education Code article yet, and entry #2 still asks for a trailer bill for something the Legislature has already passed. The sweep proposes the fixes; nothing has been written.

Sierra ran out of API credit this evening and you restored it — thank you. That is the third time (21 Aug, 22 Aug, 25 Aug). The uptime monitor did its job and raised the alert, but it only looks every three hours, so an outage can run that long before anyone is told. A balance-threshold alert on the Anthropic account itself would catch it before it becomes an outage, and that is the one thing a monitor here cannot do.

Sierra is running on Haiku 4.5 as the temporary cost measure you asked for — about a third the price of what it was on (Sonnet, not Opus). When corporate billing is released, switching back needs no code change and no session: set CPL_CHAT_MODEL on the Supabase project to claude-sonnet-4-6. Worth trying the whole-register sweep on Haiku once before you rely on it — a sixteen-row legal analysis is the hardest thing the assistant does, and it is where a smaller model would show first.

Settled, and noted so nobody undoes it: the automated check found 40 of 41 answers still correct on Haiku, and the one it dropped was the caveat beside the big waiting-credit number — the reminder that roughly a third of reviewed credit is correctly ruled Not Applicable, so the total is a ceiling rather than a debt. You said you can live with it for now, so it stays as it is. The fix is written down and ready if you change your mind: move that caveat next to the number itself instead of into a rules list further away, which would make it stick on any model.

Entry #2 (reciprocity between colleges) now asks for something already law. The new Education Code §78093.2(b)(2) requires every campus to accept transcribed prior-learning credit from other campuses. The entry still asks for a trailer bill, and it is ranked second, so it is near the top of what the Chancellor's Office reads. Two things do survive: 'no secondary review' is not stated outright, and the CSU/UC half is weaker in the statute than in the trailer bill.
